title: A City theatre lease stayed month to month for five years after its term expired

beats.text: For five years, a San Francisco theatre occupied a City basement month to month.

visual.sub: A five-year gap between the original term and the renewed lease

beats.text: Its first lease term had expired in September 2013.

visual.kicker: A five-year gap between the original term and the renewed lease

beats.text: Water had entered the building. Both sides waited for the City’s investigation.
In 2018 they moved the expiration date and exercised the extension.

visual.kicker: A five-year gap between the original term and the renewed lease

beats.text: The Real Estate Division knew of no other active lease handled this way.
The Board set the monthly base rent at $7,983.

visual.label: No common rent standard supported a market-loss estimate

beats.text: An audit found 17 nonprofit leases with nominal or no rent.

visual.kicker: No common rent standard supported a market-loss estimate

beats.text: The first pandemic waiver introduced a different problem.

visual.kicker: The first pandemic waiver carries two different figures

visual.label: The first pandemic waiver carries two different figures

beats.text: The letter amendment reversed two digits. The difference was nine dollars.

visual.label: The first pandemic waiver carries two different figures

beats.text: A second waiver covered six months in 2021.

visual.kicker: A later waiver reconciles to the tenant’s tax return

beats.text: Its tax return records $50,067 of rent forgiveness.

visual.kicker: A later waiver reconciles to the tenant’s tax return

beats.text: Federal records show separate payroll loans and a venue grant.

visual.kicker: Federal assistance records identify separate payroll and venue support

beats.text: The remaining question is which rent credits the City actually posted.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
